title: Neurologist visit
what: A doctor who treats the nervous system: brain, spinal cord, and nerves. They ask questions and check your reflexes, strength, and feeling.
why: For headaches, dizziness, back and neck pain, numbness, seizures, and sleep or memory problems.
tell_doctor: What bothers you, since when, and what helps

prepare.title: Diary
prepare.text: For headaches, write down for a few days when it hurts, how much, and what helps.

prepare.title: Scans
prepare.text: Bring MRI, CT, or EEG results and their reports, if you had them.

bring: Past test results, discharge papers, and reports
A list of your medicines, or the packs themselves
steps: The doctor asks about your symptoms
Your reflexes are checked with a small hammer
You do simple movements: close your eyes, touch your nose, walk
Strength and feeling in your arms and legs are checked
The doctor explains the next steps: treatment or tests
feel: Nothing unpleasant. The hammer taps do not hurt
Sometimes feeling is tested with a light pinprick
after: The doctor may order an MRI, an EEG, or blood tests
Do not change your treatment on your own. Ask the doctor
red_flags: A drooping face, weakness in an arm or leg, trouble speaking, or a sudden worst-ever headache: do not wait for the visit. Call emergency services

faq.a: It checks your reflexes, which shows how your nerves are working.

faq.q: Do I need an MRI before the visit?
faq.a: Usually not. The doctor will decide if you need one.

reminders.text: Neurologist visit tomorrow. Bring your scans, reports, and medicine list.
